claim: Over the registered snapshot of eligible PancakeSwap v3 pools on BSC, reading raw figures rather than displayed ones changes the published net fee rate by a measurable amount, and quoting the gross fee rate changes it by much more.
falsifier: Two results refute the claim, one per limb. If the absolute rounding gap is zero on every eligible pool, the first limb is refuted — reading displayed figures rather than raw ones would then change nothing at the precision the page prints — and the report says so. If the absolute gross gap does not exceed the absolute rounding gap on a majority of the eligible pools, the second limb is refuted. Either way the report states which of the two effects dominates by its measured median rather than by which one v1's narrative led with: a rounding gap that turns out to be noise beside the gross gap is the finding, not a disappointment, and is published as the finding.

metric.formula: For each eligible pool P in the registered snapshot, three rates from the same stored figures. net(P) = (feeUSD24h - protocolFeeUSD24h) * 365 / tvlUSD, which is docket.agents.pancake.pools.net_fee_apr, the shipped function. rounded(P) = that same function applied to feeUSD24h, protocolFeeUSD24h and tvlUSD after each has been put through the display model: scale the figure to K, M or B and keep two decimals of the mantissa. gross(P) = feeUSD24h * 365 / tvlUSD, with no subtraction. rounding_gap_pp(P) = (rounded(P) - net(P)) * 100 and gross_gap_pp(P) = (gross(P) - net(P)) * 100, both signed and both in percentage points of annualised rate. rounding_gap_relative(P) = (rounded(P) - net(P)) / net(P) and gross_gap_relative(P) = (gross(P) - net(P)) / net(P), each null where net(P) is 0 rather than a division. The reported distributions are {n, min, median, max} over the absolute value of each gap across the eligible pools, so one pool's overstatement cannot cancel another's, and every signed gap is retained in that pool's own row with the three raw figures it came from. pools_where_gross_gap_exceeds_rounding_gap = |eligible pools where |gross_gap_pp| > |rounding_gap_pp|| / |eligible pools|, reported as {numerator, denominator, value}. A pool with tvlUSD of 0 has no rate and every arm returns 0 for it; the relative distributions exclude pools whose net rate is 0 and carry the n they were computed over. Eligibility is not recomputed at scoring time: it is read from the registered snapshot, where it was fixed by docket.agents.pancake.pools.is_plausible at its shipped defaults.
metric.name: rounding_and_gross_gaps_pp
metric.units: percentage points of annualised fee rate

null_baselines.name: quote_ui_rounded
null_baselines.what_it_does: Computes the same net fee rate, with the same shipped function, over feeUSD24h, protocolFeeUSD24h and tvlUSD after each has been put through the display model in docket.advantage.v2.liquidity.ui_rounded — scale to K, M or B and keep two decimals of the mantissa. Computed by liquidity.ui_rounded_net_fee_apr and reported for every eligible pool.
null_baselines.why_it_is_the_right_null: It is the arm v1 actually observed, on one pool: a manual reader working from PancakeSwap Info computed 15.406% where the agent working from the explorer computed 15.399%. It differs from the raw arm in the rounding and in nothing else, because it calls the same function on the same three fields, and that isolation is what lets a gap be attributed to the display rather than to a second method. The display model is empirical: its whole evidence is three strings v1's manual arm read off the page — $2.06K, $3.27M and $20.59M — which are two decimals of a K/M/B mantissa and not two or three significant figures. Where the model must choose something those strings cannot settle, a mantissa that rounds up to a thousand, the choice is the model's own and the run record states whether any pool in this snapshot reaches it. This null takes no view on where a reader would have learned that the protocol takes a cut; that is the other null's subject.

null_baselines.name: quote_gross
null_baselines.what_it_does: Annualises feeUSD24h over tvlUSD on the raw figures without subtracting protocolFeeUSD24h — the fee the pool charged rather than the fee the liquidity providers keep. Computed by docket.advantage.v2.liquidity.gross_fee_apr and reported for every eligible pool.
null_baselines.why_it_is_the_right_null: It is what a reader publishes who never learns there is a split, and v1 measured it on one pool at 22.99% against a net 15.41% — half again as much yield as the position earns. It is the right null precisely because the error is not in the arithmetic: the gross figure is correctly computed and correctly annualised, and it is simply not the number a liquidity provider receives. So it is the mistake a careful reader still makes, and it is what the raw arm's subtraction is for. Its size is what the rounding gap has to be read against, and either of the two could have turned out to be the larger.

question: How far does a published net fee rate move when it is read off PancakeSwap's displayed figures rather than the explorer's raw ones, and how far does it move when the protocol's cut is never subtracted?
stopping_rule: Every eligible pool in the registered snapshot, once. No pool is re-fetched because its gap was unwelcome and none is admitted or dropped after its gap is visible: the eligible set was fixed inside the snapshot before this registration was written. The order the snapshot forced is worth stating, because it is not the order a hand-authored corpus allows. A live dataset cannot be hashed before it exists, so the snapshot was fetched first and this registration written against its digest; what was fixed before any rate was computed is the metric, the two nulls and the falsifier, and the snapshot the arithmetic ran over cannot have changed under them because the digest is cited by the run record.
